spans.s: ? Draupadī, n. of a devakumārikā (or of two? see below) in the Western Quarter: Mv 〔iii.308.9〕; LV 〔390.6〕. Mss. of both confused, and readings doubtful; Senart reads kṛṣṇā śukrā ca dr˚, the dark and light Dr.; LV may go back to some such reading; some of its mss. and Lefm.ʼs text contain kṛṣṇā. It hardly needs to be recalled that Kṛṣṇā was the name of the epic heroine known as Draupadī.
drauhiṇya (nt.), so read for ed. drauhilya, = drohiṇya, q.v., injurious malice: Śikṣ 〔279.5〕 sattva-drauhiṇyadoṣaiḥ (Tib. cited as ḥkhru baḥi ṅaṅ tshul can).
